# Historical prompt-refinement results

## Finding

The historical evidence does not demonstrate an improvement from prompt refinement. On the shared task set, direct generation has the highest acceptance rate.

## Observed results

These rates use each arm's available historical tasks and therefore have different denominators. They are descriptive, not a fair causal comparison.

| Arm | Accepted | Observed | Acceptance | Missing from union |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct generation (GPT-3.5) | 134 | 197 | 68.02% | 3 |
| Fine-tuned refiner -> GPT-3.5 | 126 | 196 | 64.29% | 4 |
| GPT-4o refiner -> GPT-3.5 | 55 | 199 | 27.64% | 1 |

## Complete-case comparison

All arms share 193 tasks. Restricting every arm to this same intersection gives:

## Paired comparisons

Differences are arm B minus arm A on their exact ID intersection. The p-value is the two-sided exact McNemar test over discordant correctness outcomes.

| Arm A | Arm B | Paired n | A only | B only | Difference | Exact p |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct generation (GPT-3.5) | Fine-tuned refiner -> GPT-3.5 | 194 | 23 | 16 | -3.61 pp | 0.3368 |
| Direct generation (GPT-3.5) | GPT-4o refiner -> GPT-3.5 | 196 | 85 | 5 | -40.82 pp | 7.53e-20 |
| Fine-tuned refiner -> GPT-3.5 | GPT-4o refiner -> GPT-3.5 | 195 | 79 | 9 | -35.90 pp | 4.15e-15 |

## Limitations

- These are historical judge observations, not a newly rerun experiment.
- Historical labels are not bound to exact provider snapshots, inference parameters, or training-artifact hashes.
- Model generations were not repeated across random seeds.
- Some arms are missing tasks; paired and complete-case counts are shown explicitly.
- Exact p-values are descriptive and are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
- Correctness on coding tasks does not measure maintainability, security, or usability.
- Likely task-identity conflicts remain in the headline history; the sensitivity analysis excludes them.
